 Home Opinion Francesco Bagnaia Aprilia Racing Ducati Malaysian Grand Prix Francesco Bagnaia will drop a bombshell about his Ducati woes the second he joins Aprilia
 Tyler Rowlinson Sun 1 November 2026 12:00, UK Add to Preferred Sources Francesco Bagnaia’s struggles at Ducati have only gotten worse in 2026, and his explanations have only gotten shorter. 
 The Italian has scored four podiums in 2026, all of which came consecutively between Barcelona and Brno. Bagnaia has not been back on the podium since then, as his woes with the GP26 have left him languishing towards the back.
 Bagnaia saw Malaysia as the last ‘concrete opportunity’ to leave Ducati on a high before he moves to Aprilia in 2027. However, it was another disappointing weekend, as he qualified down in 10th.
 Marc Marquez wins the Malaysian Grand Prix and give himself match point for the 2026 title! What did you make of that race?
 1 comment Comment Like or Comment Have your say Sign-in now for free Francesco Bagnaia will not be restricted to what he can say about his Ducati woes with Aprilia
 The two-time champion did manage to finish P6 in the Sprint, but he was miles off the pace on Sunday. He fell down the order during the race, finishing over five seconds behind the Yamaha of Alex Rins.
 Bagnaia crossed the line 13th , but that was mainly down to the retirements of Joan Mir, Diogo Moreira and Johann Zarco. After the race, he admitted that setup changes from Ducati which had fixed his problems no longer existed.
 Asked how Ducati go about helping him, Bagnaia told Sky Sports Italy : “When the problem doesn’t stem from the set-up or from an electronic calibration that you can adjust – so whether you add or reduce power, even if you make major changes – you don’t solve anything.
 “We’ve been doing this all year, and the problem has remained the same. It was the same last year. 
 Photo by Gold & Goose Photography/Getty Images “At the Misano test and the Japanese Grand Prix, something different from simple calibrations and set-up adjustments had been changed; that different element had enabled me to get back on the bike. 
 More MotoGP News “Now, unfortunately, that element clearly doesn’t exist, just as it hadn’t existed since the race after Japan last year. This morning we changed everything. We made a major set-up change and it was exactly the same, so there’s little we can do.”
 When asked to elaborate, Bagnaia said: “It doesn’t exist; let’s not go into detail.” The reporter pushed again, to which the Ducati rider replied: “Let’s not go into detail, as I said.” Asked what is the root cause of the problem, he said: “I’d really like to know.”
 This is not the first time that the Italian has been reluctant to speak about his woes. In Indonesia, Bagnaia gave an 11-word interview after he crashed out of the race, going into little detail about the issues he faced with the bike.
 Yamaha have WITHDRAWN from the Qatar Grand Prix! Give us your instant reaction!
 Comment Like or Comment Have your say Sign-in now for free READ MORE: Francesco Bagnaia and Fabio Di Giannantonio issue verdict on aiding Marc Marquez through team orders 
 Clearly, he is limited to what he can say about Ducati and what exactly is going on with him and the bike. However, that will all change the second he puts on Aprilia colours.
 Bagnaia has signed a four-year deal with the Noale outfit, and only then will everyone truly know what happened to him at Ducati over the past two years.
 The problem then will be whether or not the Italian’s exit from Ducati will give him a resurgence. After all, he is going to Aprilia on a horrendous run of form, having won just twice since Marc Marquez joined the team last year.
 Bagnaia will be Aprilia’s problem come 2027 , and it is up to them to give him a bike that he is comfortable with, and it will be up to the Italian to get back on his feet and continue the Noale outfit’s charge towards the MotoGP crown.
